purpose: Offer an exact, non-authorizing scope for one initial V0.2 baseline so the workflow can stop at REVIEW_REQUIRED until a valid V0.2 predecessor exists.

proposed_execution.trigger: One explicit workflow_dispatch after a separate authorized activation receipt and code are merged.
proposed_execution.data_authority: Reuse only the completed Crypto Core 100 dataset scope already defined by config/binance_usdm_detailed_history_v0_1_2.json and its authority receipt.

dataset_preconditions.mismatch_result: REVIEW_REQUIRED; stop before training and writes

proposed_execution.fingerprint: SHA-256 of canonical catalog-key/catalog-digest and shard receipt rows ordered by shard_index; each receipt already binds the partition object SHA-256 values.
proposed_execution.runtime: GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest isolated project environment; exact Python patch, complete installed distributions, pip/setuptools/build-install tools and available runner image metadata.
proposed_execution.existing_runtime_window: The V0.1.2 training authority remains the source/data limit. No provider fetch is included in this proposed bootstrap.

reads.purpose: Resolve exact catalog key and SHA-256
Require COMPLETE state and exact shard bindings

reads.condition: Only the catalog object referenced by the validated latest pointer
Only the 10 receipt keys referenced by the validated complete backfill state
Only partition keys referenced by those validated receipts; maximum expected 14274 objects

reads.purpose: Require no prior V0.2 baseline; if present, stop. Do not read or reuse the V0.1 latest pointer.
Fresh complete-pagination byte inventory for the existing 8000000000-byte FREE-ONLY hard stop; inspect key/size metadata only, no object payloads.

writes.condition: One run only; immutable key equality and SHA-256 readback required.
Write last only after outputs are verified; preserve training/binance_usdm/crypto-core-v0.1/latest.json unchanged.

after_bootstrap.exact_v0_2_match: NO_CHANGE; no training and no R2 write
after_bootstrap.changed_dataset_runtime_or_guard: REVIEW_REQUIRED; no automatic retraining or write under one-time authority
after_bootstrap.model_quality: Record the configured quality result; no model promotion or trading authority follows.
after_bootstrap.legacy_v0_1_pointer: Never read, migrate, overwrite, or treat as V0.2 predecessor.

acceptance_requires: Separate exact versioned activation authority and receipt, with user's explicit decision recorded, merged before workflow code changes.
GitHub-hosted Python 3.12 and 3.13 synthetic regression; production training remains pinned to the existing workflow's Python request unless a separately reviewed change.
Exact-head implementation receipt pins collector, comparator, runner, package imports, workflow, config and authority receipt.
No provider request, holdout access, source switch, pointer migration, promotion, or trading.
First bootstrap is one-time and manual; it is not natural-schedule evidence for maintenance acceptance.
